_readme: INTEGRATION FIXTURE. A test asset, not a seed: `data/` stays the
only seed directory and `scripts/seed.ts` its only reader. The
integration seed reads this directory and nothing under `data/`,
on top of a `db:seed` pass that has already written the domain.
This file carries `findings` rows for the example domain and, nested
under each, its `finding_labels` rows. Each is transcribed from the
web fixture module named in its `_comment`, so the web's fixture
path and a seeded `ar_live` tell one story. Keys beginning with an
underscore are commentary, not columns.
`fixtureId` is not a column. The database issues `findings.id`, and
the table carries no natural key, so the member keeps the `id` the
web fixture gave the row. `documentFixtureId` names a row of
`documents.json` and `entityFixtureId` one of `entities.json`, each
by its `fixtureId`; the entity is null where the finding is about
no subject the domain tracks by name.
`labels` is not a column either: each entry is a `finding_labels`
row whose `finding_id` is the finding it sits under. The web
fixture flattens a finding's labels to one `verdict`, so a finding
carries one label holding that verdict, or none where the web's
verdict is null. Every verdict is in the domain's
`verdictVocabulary`. The web fixture records no label time, so
`labelledAt` is fixed to the finding's own `createdAt` rather than
left to the column's wall-clock default, and `note` is null.

fields.summary: A public sector programme describes moving onto an event streaming platform.
End of life announced for the proprietary runtime edition, with no successor named.
Beta notes for a graph database, with a migration path from the earlier name.
The earlier name is retired in favour of the current one; benchmark results are unchanged.
A logistics operator reports a year of running the message queue in production.
The message queue reaches general availability, with a reference implementation beside it.
